record.paper_title: Discrepancy estimates for sequences: new results and open problems
record.context_brief: Metrical lower bound for hybrid sequences
record.original_question: Let x_n be the van der Corput sequence in base 2. Show that for almost all real alpha there exists a constant C(alpha) > 0 such that the discrepancy of the hybrid sequence z_n = (x_n, {n alpha}) satisfies D_N >= C(alpha) (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many N.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 Show for the discrepancy DN of the sequences (xn, {nα}n≥0) where (xn)n≥0 is the van der Corput sequence in base 2, that for almost all α there is a C(α) > 0 such that DN ≥ C(α) (log N)^2 / N holds for infinitely many N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n \ge 0$ with binary expansion $n = \sum_{j \ge 0} a_j(n) 2^j$ (where each $a_j(n) \in \{0,1\}$ and only finitely many $a_j(n)$ are nonzero), define the $n$-th element of the van der Corput sequence in base $2$ by
$$x_n = \sum_{j \ge 0} a_j(n) 2^{-j-1} \in [0,1).$$
For a real number $\alpha$, let $\{n\alpha\}$ denote the fractional part of $n\alpha$, and consider the two-dimensional hybrid sequence
$$z_n = (x_n, \{n\alpha\}) \in [0,1)^2, \qquad n = 0,1,2,\dots$$
For $N \ge 1$, let $D_N = D_N(z_0, z_1, \dots, z_{N-1})$ denote the (extreme or star) discrepancy of the first $N$ terms, i.e.
$$D_N = \sup_{B} \left| \frac{\#\{0 \le n < N : z_n \in B\}}{N} - \lambda(B) \right|,$$
where the supremum is over all axis-aligned boxes $B \subseteq [0,1)^2$ and $\lambda$ denotes the Lebesgue measure.

Prove that for almost every $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ (with respect to Lebesgue measure) there exists a constant $C(\alpha) > 0$ such that
$$D_N \ge C(\alpha) \, \frac{(\log N)^2}{N}$$
holds for infinitely many positive integers $N$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) on digital Kronecker–van der Corput hybrid sequences establishes matching upper bounds of order $(\log N)^{2+\varepsilon}/N$ for almost all $\alpha$, and proves $\Omega((\log N)^2/N)$ lower bounds only for specific $\alpha$ tied to counterexamples of an X-adic Littlewood-type conjecture. The metrical lower bound for almost every $\alpha$ for the classical van der Corput–Kronecker hybrid sequence appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Variants of the Littlewood conjecture and the exact order of the discrepancy of van der Corput–Kronecker-type sequences
status_evidence.snippet: For almost every α in [0,1], ND_N((φ_p(n),{nα})) = O(log^{2+ε} N). The Ω(log^2 N) lower bound is established only for specific α via counterexamples to the X-adic Littlewood conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Matching metric lower bound for almost all α is not established; only an upper bound and special-α lower bounds are proved.

status_evidence.title: Low Discrepancy Digital Kronecker-Van der Corput Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Provides the first known example of a low discrepancy hybrid sequence built from digital Kronecker and van der Corput sequences, with lower bounds based on ideas from Levin.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances give upper-bound constructions and special lower bounds, but not the full almost-all-α lower bound.
